direction: User: bland. add a sand dune or two and cacti
date_place: Sonoran Desert regional composite, Arizona/California borderlands, 1865-1890
reconstruction: Two small wind-sculpted dunes and cacti on adjacent stable rocky ground. This combines regional habitats for a game diorama, not a surveyed location or a claim that saguaros grow on active Imperial dune crests. Supersedes the Painted Desert location of v001 to support iconic saguaros.

sources.claim: Windblown sand from ancient Lake Cahuilla forms large natural dune fields; photographs support warm sand colour and curving crests.
Saguaros belong to the Sonoran Desert. Photographs support green ribbed columns, rounded tips and variable upward arms.
Mature saguaros can reach 45 feet; arm timing and proportions vary. Model mature plants at 5-9 metres and smaller unbranched plants.
Prickly pears occur with Sonoran cacti; photographs support branching flattened green pads with areoles and spines.

brief: Two asymmetric low dunes with curved ridges, granular golden sand and wind ripples. Strong natural green saguaros with continuous ribbed stems, rounded tips and curved ascending arms. Smaller prickly-pear groups on stable margins. Full-strength colour in existing clear warm light. No giant invented cactus proportions, flowers out of a specified season, modern objects or people.
placement: Keep all new geometry outside the central playable rectangle and away from the fuse/event routes. Ground every dune edge and cactus against the preserved source terrain. New scenery has no collision or gameplay state.
uncertainties: Arrangement, sand ripple spacing, exact RGB and individual plant ages are reconstructed.
Modern habitat and geology sources establish native forms, not an exact 1880s scene.
history_note: Sonoran saguaros grow as ribbed columns, sometimes with many upward arms. Wind moves loose sand into dunes; this game scene combines dune and stable cactus habitats.
